questions.question:
A first order, low pass filter is given with R=50 [latex]\Omega[/latex] and C=[latex]5\mu F[/latex]. What is the
frequency at which the gain of the voltage transfer function of the filter is 0.25?
questions.explanation: [latex]T.F.=\frac{V_o}{V_i}=\frac{\frac{1}{j\omega C}}{R+\frac{1}{j\omega C}}[/latex] [latex]\;\;\;=\frac{1}{1+j\omega CR} [/latex] [latex]\therefore \; \; |Gain|=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+(\omega CR)^2}} [/latex] [latex]\;\;0.25=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+(\omega \times 5 \times 10^{-6} \times 50)^2}} [/latex] On solving, [latex]\omega =15.49 \times 10^3 r/s [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\; f=\frac{15.49}{2 \pi}=2.46 kHz[/latex]
questions.topic: Magnetically Coupled Circuits, Network Topology and Filters
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]T.F.=\frac{V_o}{V_i}=\frac{\frac{1}{j\omega C}}{R+\frac{1}{j\omega C}}[/latex]
[latex]\;\;\;=\frac{1}{1+j\omega CR} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore \; \; |Gain|=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+(\omega CR)^2}} [/latex]
[latex]\;\;0.25=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+(\omega \times 5 \times 10^{-6} \times 50)^2}} [/latex]
On solving,
[latex]\omega =15.49 \times 10^3 r/s [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\; f=\frac{15.49}{2 \pi}=2.46 kHz[/latex]

questions.question: A series R-L-C circuit has R=[latex]50\Omega[/latex], L=[latex]100\mu [/latex] and C=[latex]1\mu[/latex]. The lower half power frequency of the circuit is
questions.explanation: [latex]\omega _0=\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}[/latex] [latex]\;\;=\frac{1}{\sqrt{100 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^{-6}}}=10^5 r/s [/latex] [latex]\Delta \omega =\frac{R}{L}=\frac{50}{100 \times 10^{-6}}[/latex] [latex]\;\;=50 \times 10^4 r/s [/latex] [latex]\omega _{lower}=\left [ \sqrt{\omega _0^2+\left ( \frac{\Delta \omega }{2} \right )^2}- \frac{\Delta \omega }{2}\right ] [/latex] [latex]\;\;=\left [ \sqrt{(10^5)^2+\left ( \frac{5 \times 10^5}{2} \right )^2}-\frac{5 \times 10^5}{2} \right ] [/latex] [latex]\;\;=10^5\left [ \sqrt{1+6.25}-2.5 \right ] [/latex] [latex]\;\;=0.193 \times 10^5 r/s [/latex] Hence, [latex] f_{lower}=\frac{\omega _{lower}}{2 \pi}[/latex] [latex]\;\;=\frac{0.193 \times 10^5}{2 \pi} [/latex] [latex]\;\;=3065 Hz\approx 3.055kHz[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\omega _0=\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}[/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\frac{1}{\sqrt{100 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^{-6}}}=10^5 r/s [/latex]
[latex]\Delta \omega =\frac{R}{L}=\frac{50}{100 \times 10^{-6}}[/latex]
[latex]\;\;=50 \times 10^4 r/s [/latex]
[latex]\omega _{lower}=\left [ \sqrt{\omega _0^2+\left ( \frac{\Delta \omega }{2} \right )^2}- \frac{\Delta \omega }{2}\right ] [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\left [ \sqrt{(10^5)^2+\left ( \frac{5 \times 10^5}{2} \right )^2}-\frac{5 \times 10^5}{2} \right ] [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=10^5\left [ \sqrt{1+6.25}-2.5 \right ] [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=0.193 \times 10^5 r/s [/latex]
Hence, [latex] f_{lower}=\frac{\omega _{lower}}{2 \pi}[/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\frac{0.193 \times 10^5}{2 \pi} [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=3065 Hz\approx 3.055kHz[/latex]

questions.question:
A power system consists of 2 areas (Area 1 and Area 2) connected by a single tie
line. It is required to carry out a load flow study on this system. While
entering the network data, the tie-line data (connectivity and parameters) is
inadvertently left out. If the load flow program is run with this incomplete data

options.A: The load-flow will converge only if the slack bus is specified in Area 1
options.B: The load-flow will converge only if the slack bus is specified in Area 2
options.C:
The load-flow will converge if the slack bus is specified in either Area 1 or
Area 2
options.D: The load-flow will not converge if only one slack bus is specified.

questions.explanation: For load flow study to converge there must be one slack bus in the system. As while entering the network data the tie-line data is not considered, two areas will now be treated as separate areas, hence, two slack bus (one in each area) is required.

questions.question: For the system [latex]\dot{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0\\ 0&4 \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} u; y=\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}X[/latex], with u as unit impulse and with zero initial state, the output, y, becomes
questions.explanation: [latex]x(t)=e^{At}X(0)+\int_{0}^{t}e^{A(t-\tau) }BU(\tau )d\tau [/latex] [latex]\because \;\; X(0)=0[/latex]  (as given) [latex]\therefore \;\; x(t)=0+\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2(t-\tau )} &0 \\ 0 & e^{4(t-\tau )} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\delta (t)dt [/latex] [latex]\;\;=\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2(t-\tau )}\\ e^{2(t-\tau )} \end{bmatrix}\delta (t)dt [/latex] [latex]\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t}\\ e^{4t} \end{bmatrix} [/latex] Output  [latex]y(t)=\begin{bmatrix} 4 &0 \end{bmatrix}x(t) [/latex] [latex]\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} 4 &0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t}\\ e^{4t} \end{bmatrix} [/latex] Hence, [latex]y(t)=4e^{2t}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]x(t)=e^{At}X(0)+\int_{0}^{t}e^{A(t-\tau) }BU(\tau )d\tau [/latex]
[latex]\because \;\; X(0)=0[/latex] (as given)
[latex]\therefore \;\; x(t)=0+\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2(t-\tau )} &0 \\ 0 & e^{4(t-\tau )} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\delta (t)dt [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2(t-\tau )}\\ e^{2(t-\tau )} \end{bmatrix}\delta (t)dt [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t}\\ e^{4t} \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
Output [latex]y(t)=\begin{bmatrix} 4 &0 \end{bmatrix}x(t) [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} 4 &0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t}\\ e^{4t} \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
Hence, [latex]y(t)=4e^{2t}[/latex]
